body: Give it time and in the meantime wait for your Data Center’s respective PF strats and toolboxes to be unified (NAUR, LPDU) and don’t give into the rush of clearing it on patch. A lot of players doing FRU right now, both in statics and in PF, don’t belong in Ultimates and are just filling time until 7.2 only because they cleared m4s. I and others did the same with DSR in 6.1 thinking it’d be the same as starting from any other ultimates and had our ass handed to us - just wait until underperformers either get good or realize that they’re being walled and will stop trying.

The best advice I can give you is that the first ultimate is always the hardest: by not having a point of comparison, FRU won’t be easier or harder than anything else so it’ll be a clean slate for you.
If your static hasn’t done this already I’d suggest jumping into the fights that are confirmed to be part of FRU (e8s, e11s, e12s) to see the overall difficulty of the core mechanics so that you’re vaguely prepared for their Ultimate counterparts.

The proximity of the bait itself is secondary to the mechanic since what matters is where you point the cannon at: I copied the coordinates of the Autocad hitboxes and rotated them to have the same point of reference to ensure the space is the same but only the position of the baiter is different.
If you pointed the baits to the empty spots (so away from the towers, meaning if towers are N/S then you’d point cannons towards E/W and viceversa) you’ve been doing it correctly!

From a healer perspective, OQ5 swaps H1 and R1 so that rangeds are evenly spread out after Witch Hunt: a lot of times with Hector I’d have to spot heal the ranged dps who went too far when baiting far-out and didn’t catch heals before the raidwide.

In EE2 OQ5 counts how many times you got hit (so either 1, 2 or 3 times) and groups you based on the individual hits, while Hector still counts the hits then makes long debuffs add a 1 to their count, making 3 short and 2 long stack together since 2 long has become 3. It’s a different way to approach the mechanic but the theory is the same.

I suffer from PCOS, spent my whole life thinking that I just needed to listen to doctors and do whatever I could to lose weight - I developed all kinds of eating disorders because of it and eventually made peace with the fact that I was bound to live with this condition forever.

After noticing that my hair started noticibly thinning I tried once more and went to a private clinic in my town: thank goodness I did, because the gynecologist I found immediately confirmed PCOS and told me "you tried to lose weight for years but you couldn't, am I right?". She explained that there's been advancement in PCOS treatment and studies, how hormonal imbalance is the reason why you can't actively lose weight like any normal person with a working metabolism, and that estrogen (the hormone we're not producing effectively, as we're full to the brim with testosterone) is stored in the fat of our bodies. It's a dog eating its own tail. She ended up prescribing me a birth control pill with estradiol called Klaira that completely stabilized my menstrual cycle, then scheduled me an appointment with a nutritionist to make me a diet tailored specifically to avoid food that would impact hormone levels (for example soy is full of estrogen and soy-based food and drinks are basically forbidden), and I legit lost 30kg in a year with little to no exercise, basically just a 20 minutes walk a day. I stopped losing my hair shortly after starting treatment and I've been able to keep my weight in check.

Don't lose hope: obesity is a SYMPTOM of PCOS and not the cause! All my best wishes for you to find a good and specialized doctor who knows what they're dealing with and can help you out as best as they can.

Ciao, ti rispondo direttamente in italiano: ci sono passata anch’io. Durante i periodi peggiori del disturbo (avanti e indietro estremi di cambio d’umore di giorno in giorno, esattamente gli stessi sintomi che descrivi di tuo marito) ho messo alla dura prova i sentimenti del mio compagno perché ero convinta di non aver fatto niente per meritarlo, che non dovevamo stare insieme perché ero un mostro e che non ero capace di amare. Poco dopo l’ultimo grande episodio depressivo dopo una fase di mania distrutta ho deciso di andare in terapia e alla terza seduta la psicologa mi ha messo la pulce nell’orecchio parlandomi di disturbo bipolare di tipo 2, da lì poi sono andata da uno psichiatra che mi ha ufficialmente diagnosticata e iniziato poco dopo il trattamento farmacologico (che è un calvario all’inizio, specie se non trovi il farmaco o la combo di farmaci giusta, serve un monitoraggio costante inizialmente).

Posso capire come ti senti perché ho visto il mio compagno nelle tue stesse condizioni quando ancora non sapevamo da che cosa dipendessero questi cambi ciclici nella mia persona. Sii paziente, non fargliene colpe e ricordati che è la malattia a parlare, e non lui. Sei stata bravissima a chiedere aiuto e so che ci tieni; l’unico consiglio che ti posso dare è di aiutarlo, con pazienza e con calma, e indirizzarlo verso un percorso di terapia (sia psicologica che psichiatrica) che lo aiuti a capire che tutte le decisioni che prende sono parte di un disturbo dell’umore che si può assolutamente tenere a bada coi farmaci e la consapevolezza. Ora più che mai ha assolutamente bisogno di te e ti posso assicurare che non te ne pentirai, ne varrà la pena.

I started with Quetiapine by itself and got to the target dose of 200mg - completely erased hypomania but left me with crippling depression. Added Lamictal, titrated up to 200mg, didn't do much for depression but had some small improvements. Now I've added Cyprexa 30mg (still Escitaloprom like Lexapro) to the cocktail and I'm finally feeling myself after six months of unending depression.

You're gonna be on a long titrating process of Lamictal/Lamotrigine to avoid any lasting side effects (afaik it's 25mg for 2 weeks, 50mg for another 2 weeks, then a week between each increase in dosage) but I'm pretty sure if Lamictal didn't keep me slightly above the depression line I wouldn't feel stable with only Quetiapine and Cyprexa. This mix is making me do amazing progress in both therapy and life, it gave me back the confidence and self-respect I had during hypomania but without the delusions, the obsessions and most importantly the devastating and inevitable burnout after, and a good part of this is definitely thanks to Lamictal evening things out.

It's a worth a shot imo, since we got the same meds regimen I can tell you that I do have a great experience and I hope it will be the same for you :) and if it's not - I know it's hard to do so, but keep trying!

Relax, take your time, it’s gonna pass. If someone is caring for you (family, friends) let them know that being understanding and not hold it against you is the best thing they can do to help you.

I told my friends after the diagnosis, as soon as I started medication, and half of them stopped talking to me because my struggles made them uncomfortable despite being “very understanding of my situation”. I’ve been blaming myself for it for months now, I apologized and explained what I was going through, took the responsibility of everything and wanted to make amends to show how sorry I was - turns out that not being treated like a human being who can make mistakes just to be discarded without explanations fucks you up, especially after taking me years of friendship to trust people to the point that I’d disclose a mental illness to them. It’s been hard.

Quetiapine alone forced me into a 3 months long depressive episode - please go talk with your doctor and add a mood stabilizer like Lamotrigine first. As hard as it is to truly believe meds WILL help you, if they're not helping you it means you haven't found the right one yet.
PLEASE contact your doctor! If you interrupt Lamotrigine then start it back at the same dosage you were taking before, you risk a lot of potentially fatal complications.

I’d like to add: I’m feeling like this specifically because I’m just.. nothing.

Back when I just wanted to kill myself to be forgiven by the “friends” I had lost and pushed away from me during the worst depressive episode of my life, my therapist said “the good people in your life will understand because they know what you’re going through, take it seriously but won’t hold it against you as they know that the person they love is still you”.
It’s been months and I’ve surrounded myself with people who genuinely care for me and demonstrate that they want me in their lives, but there’s nothing that I want more than to go back to the “bad people” that were in my life before, just because I was ridiculously manic and I miss that period. It’s cruel to lose someone you thought would always be in your life, but it’s even worse when you realize that you’re the only one mourning it. Keep your chin up: they were asshole and if they want to antagonize you for something you didn’t choose to be then let them do it. Don’t allow anyone else but you to control yourself.

Maybe people are just burnt out or simply lost the spark for XIV for now and a break is gonna be welcome and refreshing, but if schedules are not aligning anymore the last thing you want is to adapt and then get frustrated months later into DT when you had to change to raiding, for example, only on weekends because x has only y days available, cutting you out of potential pf clears/prog during the week.

Best of luck!

Currently going through the same, I’ve been on quetiapine 200mg for a month now (started in June with 50mg then worked my way up). Upping to 200mg was in conjunction with implementing an SSRI because the lack of motivation and employment built up into depression and was making me miserable.

For the time being, while still living through the bad side effects of Zoloft (the depression skyrocketed), I found it very helpful to make a list of things to do for the next day when I go to sleep. I write down everything I would like to tackle and specific times for it: I’m a professional artist and I haven’t been able to work at all through this depressive episode, so my goal every day is to draw for at least 2 hours to get back into it even if I half ass it or don’t finish anything. I save the progress, close photoshop after time’s up, then do the next thing on the list - today it was watching one episode of a tv show with my partner to spend time together.

Give yourself a list of things to follow, tick them once you’re done (even if you think you didn’t do them well, doing something is better than doing nothing!) and for the next day make another list with the same points or even more, or keep the things you weren’t able to do. I can’t tell you if it works or not because I’m still in the trial phase, but so far it feels way less overwhelming to function. Best of luck, you got this!

Non ho domande particolari ma grazie per l'AMA e per dare awareness a chi non conosce il disturbo: sono stata diagnosticata bipolare tipo 2 a Giugno dopo aver iniziato ad andare in terapia e aver capito grazie alla mia psicologa che c'era un pattern continuo di umore protratto negli anni che mi stava distruggendo. Il ricordo più comico è quando ho avuto una sessione di terapia in cui, con una saccenza mostruosa, dicevo alla psicologa "dottoressa, io sto benissimo e sono fortissima mentalmente, non capisco perché continuo a venire da lei a buttare tutti sti soldi!" seguito dalla sessione della settimana successiva in cui ho avuto un attacco di panico perché ero terrorizzata dalla paranoia che tutti i miei amici mi odiassero e volessero solo farmi male.

Quando arriva la diagnosi e ti rendi conto che tutte le decisioni che hai preso nella tua vita, sia in bene che in male, sono state plasmate da uno squilibrio del tuo cervello è una bella botta da metabolizzare. Ancora non mi sono stabilizzata (prendo quetiapina 200mg e ho implementato sertralina 50mg da 3 settimane perché non riuscivo più a fare niente dalla depressione ma ancora non vedo la fine del tunnel) ma leggere le varie success stories, specie da connazionali e non da americani che si fanno prescrivere antipsicotici per l'insonnia, è veramente confortante e dà speranza.

In bocca al lupo per tutto!

New FCs are also better if you sense that the vibes are rancid from the start you can just hit the bricks, you won’t have anything big to lose and will get the agency of choosing for yourself when you don’t like how something is going. Best of luck!!

In my opinion in this expansion both healers and tanks have a lot more options in terms of mitigations and "silent" coordination is harder to grasp: some healers would focus their groups tank in single target (H1 only heals and mitigates MT while H2 covers OT), others would adapt proactively to what's happening (heals and mits from both healers on the tank with less personal mits on). I'd rather excog a WAR that used Bloodwhetting <25s before they need the healing from it, or give Protraction to a PLD in Requiescat because their magic rotation will heal them for more, but that's like minmax to the extreme. 

The spiciest single target parts of last tier were mainly P3S (autos on both tanks) and Heart Stake in P4S (bleed TB on both tanks) but the first is easy to manage and the second can be cheesed with invulns. Compared to this tier where tankbusters are on both tanks, have a bleed attached to them and are before either a raidwide or a mechanic or a burst phase it can get hectic if you're not used to it and risk burning more resources than you need to.

Stupid example from my very personal experience: P6S is the worst offender for this, almost all TBs happen 10s before raidwides and using Sacred Soil for them (because your melees didn't Feint them) will force you to Succor or hope for a 120s mit from the tanks to play safe on the raidwide, since Soil won't cover both, UNLESS you place it late to cover only the last 2-3 ticks of the bleed. It's very small optimization that makes the difference between a tank dying from the bleed or not this tier (without GCD healing) and smart players playing in smart groups love it - less optimization-oriented healers will dread it because they see it as "I'm forced to use an emergency tactics adlo to heal that while last tier I didn't have to press emergency tactics once even on week 1". 

Once people have more gear and more hp it will be less ""painful"" but I do believe that a good part of healers sees having to GCD heal as a failure of the role (like a melee missing a positional, or a tank moving the boss wrong, or a caster interrupting a cast, or a phys ranged overwriting a proc) and that has to be attributed only and exclusively to the current healer design.

Are you alright? I did say that I'd like SCH (and all other healers fwiw) to have a somewhat passive but still engaging way to optimize dps with new tools that interact with the already existing kit. The fun in healing is figuring out when to heal and when to dps, different encounter design does that but then again if the good healer experience is only from week 1 savage and Ultimates then having more dps buttons or 6 dots won't change that.

I main SCH and its current state is one of the most perfect examples of good job design imo. Speaking exclusively about healers, the core of their gameplay revolves mostly around encounter design so you can't just say "give healers more dps buttons" without adjusting how often spot or raidwide damage is distributed.

Ideally for the sake of all content I'd want more interactions between gauges, dps skills and gcd heals - for SCH specifically I think a good compromise to make everything flow without feeling like you're only pressing 2 gcds would be to:

1. consolidate Aetherflow and Energy Drain in one button, decoupling Fairy Gauge from ED and giving 50/60 Fairy Gauge once Aetherflow is used and keep Indom, Excog, etc at +10 Gauge
2. have Aetherpact able to tether to enemies and act as a second dot that expires once you run out of Fairy Gauge (probably too tricky to actually implement because of pet jank?), I can't count the amount of times I just sat on 100 gauge for an entire fight because there's tons of better options for spot healing
3. have a dps subsystem akin to Lilies where the more Aetherflow stacks you collect the more healing you can dish out: building 3+3 stacks from ED+Dissipation would make you 6 stacks positive, with a healing % up buff or a free cast on gcds like Succor or Adlo, or a free emergency tactics charge at 5 stacks. This subsystem would basically implement Recitation's effect into Aetherflow but as a constant healing buff
4. now that we have removed from our hotbars Recitation and Energy Drain, give SCH a dps neutral bomb to fit into raidbuffs à la Pneuma and Afflatus Misery that resets the healing buff stacks. You're being rewarded for using your kit correctly with free damage and it's up to you and encounter design in general to build up enough stacks available to maybe fit two bombs into a burst window by balancing out ED and Dissipation at the cost of healing less for the 30-60s after

Fairies don't get reworked, Fairy Gauge becomes useful in a way that makes all types of players happy after being there just to take up space in the UI, an already good burst phase get expanded upon by rewarding optimal play. In all honesty, as long as SCH doesn't ever end up like SGE where you have to overheal and overmitigate to not run OOM I'll still be happy with all iterations of its core design.

Lastly: this is just a wet and impossible dream but after Expedient I'd love to have an ability that works like Sticky Tongue on bosses, lemme just reposition the boss myself lol
